note: Per-EVIDENCE-BRANCH capability CONTRACT, enforced by scanner/tests/test_claim_discipline.py. fact_capable/clean_capable are SEPARATE claims describing what is TRUE TODAY. target_fact_capable/target_clean_capable are what the branch MUST become — this registry is a ladder, not a ceiling. Any gap between current and target REQUIRES `blocking_work`: the concrete engineering that closes it. A gap without blocking work fails the enforcement test, so a capability can never be quietly abandoned by downgrading the claim; the claim stays, and the system is built up to meet it. Downgrading a TARGET requires an explicit `target_downgrade_rationale` stating why the capability is not achievable at all. `evidence_surface` is a CLOSED type (response_headers | response_body | transport | tls_handshake | service_response | artifact | composite | live_capture) — rules key off the declared type, never off the branch name, so a future body-derived branch cannot escape them by being called something else. `implementation_refs` point at the code that realises the branch; the enforcement test checks the referenced file and symbol actually exist. `control_requirements` is the CLOSED-vocabulary list of standing capability controls (gates / VIGIL-owned captures / instrumentation / primary-artifact parses) a branch depends on to reach its declared capability — distinct from `preconditions`, which admission evaluates per observation; for a LEAD-only branch it names the MISSING controls that `blocking_work` closes. `oracle_version` names the OracleKind whose deterministic decision procedure adjudicates a FACT on this branch — the FACT certificate binds verify.oracle_version(kind) at mint so a verifier re-runs the SAME procedure — and is EMPTY for a LEAD-only branch, which no VIGIL oracle adjudicates yet (that is its blocking_work). The manifest validator (integration/vigil_integration/live/tool_manifest.py:validate_branch_registry) enforces both columns: fact_capable ⇒ a named oracle_version, LEAD-only ⇒ none.

branches.evidence: VIGIL's OWN plain gated GET of the tool-proposed URL SERVED CONTENT DISTINGUISHABLE from a SAME-BRANCH, MULTI-SAMPLE-STABLE not-found baseline (i.e. it is not a soft-404 phantom of that shape). The baseline is built ONLY from DISTINCT NARROW-CLASS same-shape sibling controls that answered in the TARGET'S OWN response branch — every resample carrying the target's EXACT status and one shared body-hash; controls that took a different branch (a validation-reject / route-miss) are DISCARDED and controls that are unstable INSIDE the target's branch make the whole run FAIL CLOSED. Each control must also satisfy every WELL-KNOWN semantic validator the target satisfies (Luhn, base58, UUIDv4), so a checksum-constrained route accepts them instead of rejecting them. The target (resampled, stable, served) differs from that same-branch baseline BY BODY-HASH. The generated predicate AST proves the WHOLE partition offline — in-branch membership is tied to the target's status and every discarded control is proven off-branch — so the baseline cannot be cherry-picked after the fact. This is NOT a claim that the endpoint is 'live'/'real'/'exists' — only that its response is distinguishable from the same-shape, same-branch sibling baseline. The L7 analogue of the TCP tcp_handshake reachability FACT.
branches.limitation: NARROWED CLAIM: the FACT asserts EXACTLY that VIGIL's own gated GET served content distinguishable from the server's own stable, SAME-BRANCH response to randomized same-shape siblings — never 'live endpoint' / 'real resource' / 'endpoint exists'. Judged over VIGIL's OWN gated GETs of the target (resampled) + many DISTINCT NARROW-CLASS same-shape controls (each resampled); uses only RAW status codes and RAW body hashes (no decoded-body dependence). CLOSED FP classes (each MINTED a false offline-re-verifiable FACT for a NONEXISTENT url on the preceding HEAD; each is now proven at 0/80 live runs through the direct re-drive and at 0 through both the httpx and ffuf runner legs): (1) narrow-class route-miss — the control mirrors the target's EXACT per-position class/structure (hex->hex, uuid dashes preserved, base64 alphabet, numeric->numeric); an AMBIGUOUS class (e.g. all a-f letters) FAILS CLOSED. (2) bounded not-found body space (random-per-request OR per-path) — many distinct controls, each resampled, must ALL agree; a control that is unstable INSIDE the target's own status branch is AMBIGUOUS and fails the whole run closed (it is NOT silently discarded — discarding it is how a fluke 'unanimous' baseline forms out of the samples that happened to agree). (3) uniform blanket-200 (target==baseline body => LEAD). (4) path-echo (controls disagree => no baseline => LEAD). (5) CHECKSUM / SEMANTIC-VALIDATION routes (Luhn card id, base58 excluding 0/O/I/l, UUID version nibble, any internal checksum or app regex) — the sharp class, and NOT a contrived one: a random same-class control fails the route's SEMANTIC validator and takes a DIFFERENT response branch (a validation-reject) while the checksum-valid-but-NONEXISTENT target soft-404s 200, so the pre-fix predicate found the target 'distinguishable' from a baseline that was really a different branch. MEASURED pre-fix: Luhn 38/120 = 32% of runs minted a false FACT, base58 ~7%; an earlier revision of this entry framed the class as near-zero and contrived, which UNDERSTATED it — that framing is withdrawn. CLOSED in two halves: (a) VALIDATOR-AWARE CONTROLS — every control must satisfy each well-known validator the target satisfies (Luhn only on card/IMEI-length digits, base58 only on long mixed-case alnum ids, UUIDv4 only on a literal v4 UUID), so the controls land in the route's ACCEPTED set, the baseline is the route's TRUE not-found response and a checksum-valid phantom is seen to MATCH it => LEAD, while a genuinely distinguishable id still mints; narrowing the control set can only cost controls => the floor => fail closed, never a wrong contrast; (b) the SAME-BRANCH BASELINE, which covers every validator VIGIL does NOT know — the baseline is built ONLY from controls whose every resample carried the TARGET'S EXACT status with one shared body-hash, the target is distinguished BY BODY within that branch (never across a reject branch), every discarded control is PROVEN off-branch by a clause of the same predicate AST, and fewer than the floor of in-branch controls FAILS CLOSED to a LEAD. If the last path segment cannot be confidently mirrored (root/directory URL, ambiguous class, or a mirror space too small) the FACT FAILS CLOSED. CONSEQUENCE (honest): a HARD-404 server (one that returns a genuine 404 for well-formed nonexistent same-shape siblings) yields NO same-branch served baseline, so a real endpoint there is a LEAD, not a FACT — this branch mints only where the not-found response is SERVED (a soft-404-style branch). Likewise a checksum route with an UNKNOWN validator yields too few in-branch controls => LEAD. Both are lost true positives, not false ones. RESIDUAL (the one class that genuinely remains, and it is IRREDUCIBLE for a black-box same-class method): an APP-SPECIFIC validator VIGIL cannot know whose REJECT lives INSIDE the target's own same status branch — a route answering 200 with body V for an id it considers invalid and 200 with a DIFFERENT body N for a valid-but-nonexistent one. The same-shape controls (mostly invalid) then form a stable in-branch baseline V that the nonexistent target (N) differs from, and the FACT mints for a phantom. It cannot be closed by any observation of this kind: that capture is structurally IDENTICAL to the legitimate case this branch exists for (a real endpoint on a server whose same-shape siblings all soft-404 with one uniform body), so any rule that refused it would also refuse every true positive. It is therefore (i) named in the FACT's own note, (ii) pinned by test_unknown_in_branch_validation_reject_is_the_documented_irreducible_residual, and (iii) bounded: it shrinks as (1-p)^N_CONTROLS in the validator's acceptance rate p, because any in-branch control that lands on the target's own body breaks the baseline's unanimity => LEAD, so raising _LIVENESS_CONTROLS trades traffic for it, and it is nil for the well-known validators above. Under the narrowed claim a special-cased error page for a phantom id (distinguishable served content) is a TRUE-if-modest statement, not an overclaim. A CLEAN is a channel-confirmed hard not-found (404/410) at the EXACT probed URL on every resample, control-independent, BOUNDED to that URL only — NEVER an enumeration-completeness claim. A 401/403/405/5xx target is INCONCLUSIVE.

The achieved-state predicate oracle fires ONLY when ALL hold: the attacker's cross-read is a SUBSTANTIVE SUCCESS (2xx with real content — not empty/error/soft-deny); the discriminator is in the victim's authoritative (also substantive) record; the attacker's cross-read reached that SAME discriminator; the discriminator is ABSENT from the attacker's OWN substantive control object (control_ref, mandatory) — absence-in-an-error is NOT proof; it is ref-independent; it is ABSENT from a logged-out baseline that is a valid gating proof; AND — decisively (round-5) — it is ABSENT from a same-ref UNAUTHORIZED-AUTHENTICATED baseline that is a SUBSTANTIVE SAME-SHAPE read: a THIRD attacker-controlled principal that also lacks access, whose read is a 2xx that RENDERED the same object (the same class as the attacker's substantive cross-read), NOT a 401/403 denial. Clause (c) is the anti-reflection proof a single body's content heuristics could NOT give: a per-object REFLECTED token (a public slug/uuid echoed into an authenticated 200 soft-deny — no bare-error phrase, not a literal substring of the ref) is echoed by ANY same-shape render of the object, so it appears in the same-shape unauthorized-authenticated baseline TOO, its absent-clause fails, and NOTHING mints — only a datum PRESENT in the attacker's read yet ABSENT from a peer's same-shape read of the same object (genuinely access-gated) fires. A 401/403 DENIAL is NOT a valid clause-(c) control: a denial never renders the object, so a reflected token is absent from it VACUOUSLY (absent because unrendered, not because private) — accepting a denial was the round-4 hole a reflected slug rode into a durable false FACT, closed in round-5 by requiring a substantive same-shape baseline. All re-derived offline over the retained bodies+statuses; a reflected token in a same-shape baseline, public content, a 403 attacker read, shared boilerplate, a NON-substantive read, a denial-only or non-substantive unauthorized-authenticated baseline, or a MISSING baseline all correctly do NOT fire.
